item.title: Hop in: We're taking a pop culture road trip on Route 66
item.description: Route 66 is celebrating 100 years of being the country's most famous highway. This icon of American culture passes through eight states — and has shown up for decades in movies, books, music and art.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Rosalía and Milo J take top awards as Daddy Yankee is paid tribute at Latin Grammys
item.description: The night was filled with music and surprises. Rosalía opened the show with medley of tracks and elaborate dancing, and Milo J appeared with a colorful Uruguayan theatrical ensemble.

item.title: People getting hot and bothered over newly-elected Democratic men
item.description: You may have noticed that a lot of people on social media are getting really hot and bothered over the newly-elected Democratic men. It says a lot about how Democrats have responded to the Trump era.

item.title: Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?
item.description: As Trump's arch and other projects make their way through the courts, many critics are looking to Congress to stop them. Democrats have a few tools, including funding and oversight.

item.title: 'We Chose to Go to the Moon' is a radical retelling of the history of the space race
item.description: Last April, a concert at Carnegie Hall brought the history of the space race to life using Broadway stars, an orchestra, film footage and still photos. Now, PBS is televising the exciting production.

item.title: From the firehouse to a Bronx pawn shop, Steve Buscemi is a lifelong New Yorker
item.description: Buscemi worked as a NYC firefighter for four years while he was getting his start in theater and stand-up comedy. He's appearing in two new films: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York and Wild Horse Nine.

item.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Actor Stacy Keach, who played a private eye and plenty more, dies at 85
item.description: Known as TV's detective Mike Hammer, Keach was a prolific actor on stage and screen. His wide-ranging roles included cops, cowboys and Shakespearean characters.
